title: Differential transcendence of nonzero field-valued second-order difference solutions over characteristic-zero fields satisfying property P
source_title: Differential transcendence criteria for second-order linear difference equations and elliptic hypergeometric functions
author: Carlos E. Arreche; Thomas Dreyfus; Julien Roques
difficulty_reason: Standard Picard--Vessiot theory and the cited Galois classification only reduce the equation to primitive and imprimitive alternatives. The author must transfer a nonzero differentially algebraic solution to the parametrised Picard--Vessiot setting and exclude the imprimitive branch through a change-of-basis determinant and the Riccati/telescoper obstructions. In the primitive branch, the scalar Galois action and differential-polynomial evaluation yield a separate contradiction, with every nonzero-solution step retained in the selected field-extension scope.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem3.5 restricted to solutions in (sigma,delta)-FIELD extensions of K, rather than arbitrary potentially nonreduced K-algebras. Characteristic0, algebraically closed sigma constants C, commuting automorphism/derivation, and propertyP are essential: K is C1 and has no nontrivial finite extension to which sigma extends. Both absence of a K Riccati solution and absence of a nonzero C[delta] telescoper are retained. Complete new Lemma3.4 reduction and full imprimitive/scalar-group contradiction read. Standard Picard–Vessiot theory, Galois classification and Kolchin evaluation are explicit named prerequisites. Printed theorem equation a(y) is a bounded dropped-sigma typo; reference3.1 and both adjacent companion matrix and proof consistently mean a sigma(y). No claim for general nonreduced coefficient algebras or a separate elliptic-hypergeometric instance.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: Parametrized difference Galois groups, irreducible/imprimitive dichotomy and scalar differential-group action yield a practical Riccati/telescoping transcendence criterion.
